record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional BCS problem, prove the analog of the two-dimensional convergent-contribution result, namely that the sum of all convergent contributions is analytic in the coupling constant.

evidence.quote: To find the analog of [FMRT1][DR2], namely that the sum of all “convergent contributions” to the theory is analytic in the coupling constant remains in our opinion a major challenge of constructive theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional BCS model of interacting non-relativistic fermions on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or $\mathbb{Z}^3$) at finite temperature $T>0$, with a spherical Fermi surface and a short-range attractive pair interaction of coupling constant $\lambda$. Following the constructive renormalization-group approach, decompose the propagator into scales and classify the perturbative contributions to the connected Schwinger functions into "convergent" contributions (those whose graphs do not contain two- or four-point subdiagrams requiring renormalization, i.e., the non-superficially-divergent part of the expansion after suitable resummation of the leading BCS instability).

Prove the three-dimensional analog of the known two-dimensional result for Fermi liquids with non-nested, non-degenerate Fermi surfaces: namely, show that the sum of all convergent contributions to the model is analytic in the coupling constant $\lambda$ in a domain of the form
$$\{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : |\lambda| \le c / |\log T|^{k}\}$$
(for some explicit $k$ and constant $c>0$) uniformly as $T\to 0^+$, with the sum defining a well-defined analytic function of $\lambda$ in that domain.
artifact.status_search_result: Analyticity of convergent contributions has been established in two dimensions (e.g., for the half-filled Hubbard model and for jellium-type 2D Fermi liquids by Feldman–Magnen–Rivasseau–Trubowitz and Disertori–Rivasseau). The 3D BCS analog is described in the constructive-field-theory literature as a major outstanding challenge, and no proof of analyticity of the sum of all convergent contributions in the coupling constant has been published. The problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: The Two Dimensional Hubbard Model at Half-Filling. I. Convergent Contributions
status_evidence.snippet: Analyticity theorems in the coupling constant established for the 2D model at half-filling; convergent contributions shown analytic in λ.
status_evidence.claim: The 2D analyticity result for convergent contributions exists; the 3D analog is what the problem asks for.

status_evidence.title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the analog of the 2D convergent-contribution analyticity result for the 3D BCS problem as a major open challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is stated as open in the constructive field theory community.
